title: Which Words Hide in the Grid?

concept.title: Search for all words at once with a trie
body: Searching a grid for **one** word is a simple backtracking. For many words, repeating that search for every word wastes time, because words share beginnings. A **trie** (prefix tree) stores all the words together: each node stands for a prefix, each step to a child adds one letter, and a node can be marked "a word ends here".

Now one search from each cell walks the grid and the trie **at the same time**: from a cell with letter `ch`, go to the child `ch` of the current trie node. If there is **no such child**, no word starts with this prefix and the path is cut at once. If the node ends a word, record that word, and continue (longer words may share the path).

The prefix cut makes this fast: the search follows only roads that can still become one of the words. A cell is marked with `#` while it is on the current road (letters never equal `#`), which is the same as a table of visited cells.

statement: A grid of lowercase letters and a list of words are given. A word is *in the grid* if its letters can be read by walking from cell to neighbouring cell (above, below, left or right) without using any cell twice. Print all words of the list that are in the grid, in alphabetical order, one per line. If none is in the grid, print `-1`.
inputFormat: Each of the next `r` lines has `c` letters.
The next line has `k`, the number of words.
The last line has the `k` words.
outputFormat: The words found, in alphabetical order, one per line, or `-1`.
constraints: 1 <= k <= 20; the words are different and have 1 to 7 letters

examples.input:
3 3
oaa
etn
ihk
4
oath pea eat rain
examples.note: The words oath and eat are in the grid.

hints: Build a trie of all the words.
Walk the grid and the trie together; stop when the trie has no child for the next letter.
Mark the cells of the current road, and record a word when the trie node ends one.

starter.python:
r, c = map(int, input().split())
grid = [input().strip() for _ in range(r)]
k = int(input())
words = input().split()

# Your code here

explanation: A trie holds all the words. Starting from every cell, the search follows the grid and the trie together, stops when the trie has no child for the next letter, records the word of every node that ends one, and marks and unmarks the cells of the current road.
solution.complexity: Time O(cells * 4 * 3^(L-1)) in the worst case, far less in practice; space O(total length of the words).
